Subject: Subprocessor list and security follow-up

Hi Jane —

Thanks again for the time today. Quick recap and next steps from our side:

- Recap: we covered architecture (API + optional private deployment), data residency options, and high-level perf/cost expectations.
- You asked for: 1) current subprocessor list, 2) SOC 2 status/report access, and 3) vendor security questionnaire to start the evaluation.

Next steps we will take:
- I attached our current subprocessor list (redwood_subprocessors_20270404.pdf). It includes cloud providers and third-party services we commonly use.
- I created a short vendor questionnaire link for Acme: https://redwoodinference.app/vendor-questionnaire/ACME-789 (also attached as a text stub).
- Neha (cc'd) is our security lead and will follow up on any technical clarifications (encryption, key management, BAA options).

Couple of notes based on our call:
- Data sharing boundaries: by default, customer data is isolated per-tenant and stored in encrypted buckets. We only share data with subprocessors listed in the attachment (no training on customer data without explicit agreement).
- Cloud providers: primary infra is AWS (us-west-2) with optional GCP regions; object storage is AWS S3 (encrypted).
- Compliance: we can provide SOC 2 summary/report access and discuss HIPAA BAAs where required.

If you can confirm the best email for the security questionnaire and whether you need a signed NDA/BSA first, we can get that started today.

Thanks — looking forward to the next steps.

—
Marissa Cole
Enterprise Security & Programs
Redwood Inference

Hi Marissa —

Thanks for the recap and the files. A couple of follow-ups from our security team:

1) SOC 2: do you have a Type II report (and if so, is there a summary we can share with internal reviewers)?

Hi Jane —

Great questions — answers below and attached materials.

1) SOC 2: Redwood completed SOC 2 Type II (Security) in Q4 2025. We cannot attach the full report to an unvetted thread, but you can review a redacted summary at: https://redwoodinference.secure/soc2/2025-report. If Acme needs the full report, we can arrange access via our secure portal (we typically require an NDA or third-party request form).

2) HIPAA / BAA: We support HIPAA-covered workloads and will sign a BAA with customers that require it. Neha (cc) manages BAAs — she can kick off the standard BAA template and confirm any specifics for PHI handling.

3) Subprocessors / third-party risk: the attached PDF lists primary subprocessors. High-level callouts:
   - Cloud infra: AWS (EC2, EBS, S3 in us-west-2) and optional GCP (us-central1) for certain regions.
   - Edge / CDN: Cloudflare (DDoS/proxy).
   - Monitoring & observability: Datadog (metrics/logs), Sentry (errors) — logs are redacted and access-controlled.
   - Managed services: a small set of vendor partners for ops automation (names in the attached file).
   - Sub-subprocessors: we do use a couple of contractors for hardware ops in specific regions; none process customer data outside the subprocessors listed. We will confirm APAC processing specifics if you have region-specific residency needs.

4) Key management / encryption: data at rest is encrypted by default. We support customer-managed KMS keys (bring-your-own-key) for Dedicated and Private deployments; for Hosted, we offer KMS integrations (AWS KMS) with customer CMK options for enterprise plans.

5) Questionnaire link: you can start here — https://redwoodinference.app/vendor-questionnaire/ACME-789 — I've also attached a small text stub (redwood_vendor_questionnaire_link.txt) with the link for internal distribution.

Attachments included: redwood_subprocessors_20270404.pdf, redwood_vendor_questionnaire_link.txt

If you want, we can schedule a short follow-up with Neha to walk through the questionnaire answers and any technical deep-dive (30 min). Rafael and Monica are on the thread to route procurement/contracting questions.

Thanks —
Marissa
